answer.rationale: Competitive pricing pressure on SMB is immediate, but memory_73 shows promotional pricing materially reduced 30-day retention despite acquisition lift—a critical risk given primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Memory_44 demonstrates enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows with superior pipeline quality. Rather than defend SMB on price (a losing race), redirect sales resources to accelerate enterprise pipeline as a hedge against SMB churn. This preserves revenue quality, leverages proven conversion channel, and avoids the retention damage pattern of promotional pricing. SMB churn is real but memory_31 and memory_86 show activation improvements (simplification, onboarding, messaging) can address retention through product quality and engagement—these are lower-risk, non-price levers to implement in parallel at small scale while enterprise sales assist absorbs leadership urgency. This approach acknowledges competitive pressure without betting long-term health on unsustainable pricing.
